title: Internal Hom from a coherent module into an injective module is flasque
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]), let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal I$ be an injective $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Then the underlying sheaf of abelian groups of $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] is flasque on the Zariski topological space of $X$ [def-sc-zariski-flasque].

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA (cohomology-lemma-injective-restriction-surjective: injectives are flasque; the same argument with the extension by zero of F|_U gives the sheaf Hom case), as used in the proof of Lemma 0FZ3 (1) via the local-to-global Ext spectral sequence

proof.text: Fix opens $U'\subset U\subset X$ and write $j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ and $j_{U'}:U'\hookrightarrow X$. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], sections of $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I)$ over an open $V$ are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_V}(\mathcal F|_V,\mathcal I|_V)$. The extension-by-zero adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-module-extension-by-zero-adjunction] identifies this group with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j_{V!}(\mathcal F|_V),\mathcal I)$ via $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta)|_V$ (clause (2) of that node).

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA proof, the extension-by-zero/Yoneda identification of sections

proof.text: The inclusion $U'\subset U$ gives a morphism (on the presheaves $j_{p!}$ it is the identity on $V\subseteq U'$ and $0$ otherwise, then sheafify) $j_{U'!}(\mathcal F|_{U'})\to j_{U!}(\mathcal F|_U)$. It is a monomorphism: by the stalk clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-extension-by-zero-adjunction], at a point outside $U'$ the source stalk is zero, while at a point of $U'$ both stalks identify with the corresponding stalk of $\mathcal F$ and the map is the identity; applying [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (5) to the complex $0\to j_{U'!}(\mathcal F|_{U'})\to j_{U!}(\mathcal F|_U)$, which is exact on stalks at every point, shows it is exact at the source, i.e. the map is a monomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA proof, the canonical map between extensions by zero and its stalkwise injectivity

proof.text: Since $\mathcal I$ is injective, [def-sp-injective-resolutions] says that precomposition with this monomorphism induces a surjection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j_{U!}(\mathcal F|_U),\mathcal I)\twoheadrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(j_{U'!}(\mathcal F|_{U'}),\mathcal I)$. Under the bijections of Step 1, this is exactly the restriction map (elementary: the map of Step 2 restricts on $U'$ to the identity of $\mathcal F|_{U'}$ through $\theta$, so both routes send $\psi$ to $(\psi\circ\theta)|_{U'}$) $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I)(U)\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal I)(U')$.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA proof, injectivity applied to the extension-by-zero monomorphism

proof.text: The restriction map is surjective for every inclusion of opens $U'\subset U$. Therefore the underlying abelian sheaf is flasque by [def-sc-zariski-flasque].

proof_origin.place: Cohomology, Lemma 01EA and its proof, with the same argument applied to sheaf Hom

split_report.summary: Split the proof into the extension-by-zero description of Hom sections, stalkwise monomorphism for nested opens, injective lifting, and the flasque definition. The existing module extension-by-zero adjunction is used as a generic tool; no new nodes were needed.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes the parenthetical Ext-vanishing proof's injective-resolution input: the Cohomology Lemma 01EA restriction-surjectivity argument, with j_! applied to the restricted coherent module.

tool_uses.why: Its adjunction and stalk statement identify Hom sections with maps from extension-by-zero modules and establish the needed stalkwise monomorphism.
Its statement supplies the stalkwise injectivity criterion used to prove the extension-by-zero map is monic.
